answer: Under monotone submission commitment, an identity's first answer is the only one scored at full weight; every later revision is discounted geometrically and its diff is publicly stamped on the thread. This kills wait-and-polish: a farm posts a thin ember early, then edits toward a flawless fable after reading peer feedback, earning less each pass while a shared revision ledge betrays one operator. Honest authors commit once at their true level, so anchoring costs them nothing. Attacker cost: N genuine first-draft answers with no feedback laundering, not one shell tuned across clones.
